A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MLVU and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. The renamed title, reformatted layout, and relocation of earlier results to the development-set appendix can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 20 MLLMs, including task scores, Time-ladder experiments, component analyses, and retrieval-augmented generation experiments.

after.justification: V3 reports original test-set evaluations of 23 MLLMs, development-set results, and analyses of clip position, action counts, and other performance factors.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction approach, inference templates, and auxiliary retrieval-augmented generation procedure are retained. V1 Appendix G and v3 Appendix H describe the same LanguageBind clip embeddings, similarity-based top-K retrieval, and clip concatenation, with identical RAG settings and results.

E1.justification: V3 broadens represented video domains by adding tutorials, sports, and life records to the collection described in v1 Appendix B. Section 3.2.2 also adds CLEVRER alongside WebVid as a source of needle clips. These expand data coverage while retaining the nine task categories.

E2.justification: The development-set comparison adds ShareGPT4Video, VideoLLaMA2, LongVA, Video-CCAM, and Video-XL, while removing the standalone InternVL-1.5, GPT-4 Turbo, and Video-ChatGPT rows from v1 Table 1. Some removed comparators remain in other analyses. The new test comparison additionally includes InternVL-2 and LLaVA-Onevision. VideoLLaMA2 is distinct from the retained Video-LLaMA-2.

E3.justification: V1 explicitly specifies no development/test split. V3 retains its 2,593 questions as a development set and adds a 509-question test set, using six answer choices instead of the development set's four. New analyses group referring clips into position quartiles and action-count questions into probe-count intervals. Accuracy and generation-scoring criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 Figures 4–5 add analyses of sensitivity to referring-clip position in ego reasoning and plot QA, and difficulty as the number of action probes increases. The duration analysis is revised, while v1's detailed Time-ladder Tables 7–9 and per-task duration plots are removed. Context-length, backbone, and RAG analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for model scores. The added plots continue to present point estimates; their markers do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive test-set results, including GPT-4o's 54.5 M-Avg and 5.87 G-Avg, and new development-set results such as Video-XL's 64.9 M-Avg. GPT-4o's original 64.6 and 5.80 development scores are retained, so the test scores do not establish a same-setting decline. New diagnostic findings are added, and detailed Time-ladder result entries are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops a theorem or proof framework. The mathematical description of RAG embeddings and retrieval, along with the evaluation scoring rules, is unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a diverse, nine-task benchmark for long-video understanding. One headline empirical takeaway changes: v1 emphasizes a persistent large gap between open-source and proprietary models, whereas v3's introduction emphasizes recent long-video models narrowing that gap. The principal benchmark claims and conclusion otherwise remain.

C2.justification: V3 replaces v1's pessimistic interpretation of long-video models with an account of recent progress, interprets positional robustness as improved retrieval and reasoning, and links increasing probe counts to difficulty integrating multiple details. It also removes the explicit limitations concerning high-resolution videos, tracking, and low-level processing. The RAG limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 removes v1's backbone and checkpoint-link tables, exact GPT API version identifiers, repository and dataset access links, and licensing, hosting, maintenance, and datasheet sections. It adds updated collection counts and model release dates but supplies substantially less reproducibility and access information. This documents removed disclosures, not evidence that online resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands comparative positioning through Table 1, explicitly contrasting MLVU with existing and concurrent benchmarks, including newly cited Video-MME and LongVideoBench. Related work adds context-extension approaches such as LWM, LongVA, and Video-XL, while the earlier LVU dataset discussion and citation are removed.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, introductory and related-work passages are edited, and the results discussion becomes numbered findings. Development results move to an early appendix, and several appendix sections are removed or reorganized. The main section sequence and much of the construction, annotation, RAG, and conclusion wording are preserved.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1 with a genre hierarchy and task blocks, adds benchmark-comparison and split-distribution tables, and introduces two diagnostic figures. Results tables gain release-date and random-reference rows, development results move to the appendix, and the Time-ladder display becomes an aggregate plot. Several earlier tables and figures disappear.

improvement.justification: The broader coverage, updated comparators, separate test set, and targeted diagnostics strengthen empirical usefulness. However, v3 removes important reproducibility information and detailed supporting results, and introduces visibly inconsistent entries in main Table 2: Video-LLaVA's summarization score is 20.9 and Qwen-VL-Max's captioning score is 20.0 despite stated maxima of 10. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain from the supplied PDFs.
